title: From Food Deserts to Fresh Food: The Role of Digital Accessibility in Nutrition Assistance Programs
near_miss_reason: Time-varying controls are the sole violation of the staggered state-month specifications: the Callaway-Sant'Anna estimates of Table 6 and Figure 2 (csdid with not-yet-treated controls, state as unit, 12 launch-month cohorts April 2019-May 2022) include the time-varying state-month COVID covariates cases, deaths, mask_mandate and stay_at_home (Stata code.do lines 300-335). The household-level regressions of Tables 3-5, 7, 9-14 and Figure 1 add household demographics and treat x policy interactions on top of the controls and so fail a further rule. Staggered binary design: SNAP Online Purchasing Pilot launched at state-specific months; all states adopt by May 2022 (no never-treated states). NielsenIQ-derived data are not shipped.
eligible_reason: The underlying design qualifies: the SNAP Online Purchasing Pilot launched in states at 12 distinct months between April 2019 and May 2022 (hard-coded gvar in data_construction.sas lines 357-387), treatment is binary and absorbing (post = year_month > gvar), and Table 6 / Figure 2 report Callaway-Sant'Anna (csdid, notyet) at the state-month level with state as the unit. But no reported specification is eligible as published: the csdid runs include time-varying COVID covariates (cases, deaths, mask_mandate, stay_at_home), and the household-level TWFE regressions (Tables 3-5, 7, 9-10, 12-14) include time-varying household demographics, state-level COVID controls, and treat x (stimulus/stay-at-home/mask/cases/deaths/SNAP-increase) interactions (additional treatments). Moreover the main analysis data (item_month_balance, item_month_state) are derived from NielsenIQ Consumer Panel data and are not in the package. Strictly ineligible; candidate csdid specs listed under ineligible_specs.
design_notes: Stata code (Data and Code/Stata code.do, 350 lines) run on SAS-built datasets. Household-month panel item_month_balance: treat = SNAP-income-eligible household (by Household_Income x Household_Size bins, lines 38-55; alternative bandwidths at lines 173-281), post = state launch (from SAS), spec: reghdfe Y stay_at_home act i.demographics c.treat#c.post c.treat#c.act c.treat#c.act2 c.treat#c.act3 c.treat#c.stay_at_home c.treat#c.increase c.treat#c.mask_mandate c.treat#c.cases c.treat#c.deaths, absorb(Household_Cd state_month) cluster(Fips_State_Cd), sample 2018m4-2022m10 (Tables 3-4 at lines 90-99; headline 7.1% fresh-food effect is Table 4). Figure 1 (line 104): treat x relative-period dummies (period = year_month - gvar2 + 65, base 28) with the same controls. Table 5: food-desert subsample. Table 7: nonfood placebo. Table 8: New York only, single date (post_ny), household FE + year-month FE. Table 9: falsification with fake_post. Table 12-13: entropy, large-retailer share, junk food. Table 14: heterogeneity by digital accessibility (coverage_level) and habit tercile. Table 6 / Figure 2 (lines 292-335): csdid on state-month aggregates separately for SNAP-eligible and non-eligible households, with covariates, notyet controls; event_plot. Table 11 (lines 339-348): Instacart zip-month data, low_income x post with time-varying controls, absorb(state_month postal_code). All 50 states + DC have a launch date, so there are no never-treated states; csdid uses not-yet-treated controls. Launch cohorts (year_month index): 16 (NY, 2019m4), 26 (WA, 2020m2), 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34 (2020m4-2020m10), 40 (ME, 2021m4), 52 (LA, MT, 2022m4), 53 (AK, 2022m5).

Record coded under the earlier rule with no near_miss field. Added eligible=false so code/17 picks the flag up. Data not shipped.
